video.title: The Side Hustle AI Was Supposed to Kill Is Booming

summary: Host Chris Koerner interviews freelance writer Steph Spectre about charging tech companies for AI-assisted, research-heavy articles. Spectre describes using AI for selected steps while relying on hands-on product research, personal experience and editing to produce the final work. She also discusses other writing and coaching work, finding clients through Upwork and tailored outreach, and setting project prices after clarifying scope. The central takeaway is that AI can speed up parts of writing, but human judgment and distinctive experience remain valuable to clients.

speakers.name: Steph Spectre
speakers.description: Freelance writer and former employee of Apple and Zapier.

ideas.name: Freelance writing for technology companies
ideas.one_liner: Write researched, search-oriented articles and tutorials for technology companies, using AI for selected research and drafting steps and editing the final work as a human.
ideas.business_model: Per-article project fees, with potential to expand a client relationship into recurring writing and related work.
ideas.customer: B2B software companies such as Zapier, Jotform and Softr that need articles, comparisons, alternatives pages or product tutorials.
ideas.problem: Companies need timely, useful content that explains software and targets search terms, while still reflecting real product use and human judgment.
ideas.offer: Research and write technology articles, often including product comparisons, alternatives pages and step-by-step tutorials. Related work can include uploading posts, website copy and emails.

pricing.model: Per-article project pricing; some early or other projects may be hourly.

price_points.label: Range stated while describing monthly workload; upper figure interpreted from the transcript's 'to,200'
Rates she said she was seeing on Upwork

pricing.notes: She prefers project-based quotes after clarifying scope. The host's $1,000 figure is a framing question; her stated rate range is $900–$1,200 per post.

acquisition_channels.details: She started on Upwork, got her first client there, and still uses it. When searching, she sometimes aims to apply to 10 carefully selected jobs a day, choosing work she can tailor a pitch to and that may grow into a larger contract.

quote.text: When I do look for jobs, I'll get into little moments where I'll go, "Okay, I'm going to apply to 10 jobs a day."
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

acquisition_channels.details: She pitches companies directly, including highlighting her background and ability to publish quickly when a topic becomes timely. Transcript does not specify the method used for each pitch.

quote.text: How much do you think that plays into these tech companies hiring you? Huge. Yeah, I think people and I play that up in cover letters or when I do just cold pitches to to people.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

acquisition_channels.details: She recommends being active on social platforms, commenting and engaging with prospective clients, and making a specific human connection. She says LinkedIn or another platform where the freelancer is active can be used.

quote.text: If you're not on freelancing sites, getting on social media and just whether it's LinkedIn or wherever it is that you're active and commenting, engaging directly, messaging people, it doesn't have to be gross.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

acquisition_channels.details: She recommends asking friends or family whether they know someone who needs writing help. She also describes repeat work growing from a good relationship with a client.

quote.text: if you you ask a family or a friend for hey do you know anybody who's starting a business or just need help needs help with their writing.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

ideas.delivery: The writer signs up for and tests the products being covered, researches relevant discussions and pricing, may capture screenshots, then writes the article. For tutorials, she has recorded her screen and narration, used Cursor to route video and audio processing to Gemini, and used Claude to draft from notes and a template. She edits the draft herself and may upload the finished post for the client.
unit_economics_claims: She says a typical article takes five to six hours and is around 2,500 to 3,000 words.
She says she currently writes five to ten posts per month at roughly $800 to $1,200 per post and earns close to $6,000 to $7,000 per month across writing, coaching and editing.
She says roughly 70–80% of the words in an article are hers, while the structure is typically hers.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. She says she got her first freelance client through Upwork after starting in 2016, but gives no elapsed time.

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings and inbound search can reduce manual lead collection, but choosing jobs and writing tailored pitches require human judgment. UK-compliant corporate cold email can be partly automated with careful list screening and opt-out handling; unsolicited messages to individuals and sole traders require consent.

onboarding.how: Forms, call transcription and AI summaries could collect project context, but a human should clarify goals, scope and access to the software being covered.

delivery.how: AI can process recordings, summarize research and draft from templates, but the writer tests products, judges what matters, adds experience and edits the output.

billing.how: Invoices and payment reminders are routine software tasks once the project scope and fee are approved.

support.how: Agents could handle routine status questions, but revisions and technical or editorial feedback need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: The service model applies in the UK. Client demand, prices and examples may differ, and outreach must follow UK rules: unsolicited marketing emails and DMs to individuals and sole traders generally require consent; cold email to limited companies can be used subject to applicable requirements.

risks: Automating the entire process can create setup and maintenance work, leave output below standard and contribute to burnout.
Clients may expect real product knowledge, accuracy and fast publication when news or product changes create a timely content opportunity.
A writer who relies entirely on AI may produce generic work and limit the development of their own voice and skills.
The transcript gives personal rate and workload claims but does not provide contracts, costs, revision terms or client retention data.

tactics.name: Build a small, relevant writing portfolio
steps: Choose a writing format and subject area to demonstrate.
Create four or five samples; she suggests three blog posts, a landing page and another format as one possible mix.
Publish the work on a professional-looking site. She says publication by an established outlet is not required.
Use samples to demonstrate range and give prospects something concrete to review.

quote.text: So, you don't need a some kind of a certification but you want to have produced I would say four maybe five pieces of writing.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

tactics.name: Use Upwork to find early work and recurring clients
steps: Create a portfolio and apply for relevant jobs on Upwork.
When searching actively, choose up to 10 jobs a day that are interesting and offer a specific explanation of how you can help.
Look for one-off jobs that could lead to recurring needs, such as a company requesting one article that may need more.
Once trust is established, offer related work such as uploading the posts.

quote.text: So, I can pitch that or they might just ask me, I can also offer to upload the blog posts myself, which is another great way to expand the contract
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

tactics.name: Write a tailored, human cold pitch
steps: Keep the pitch to roughly four or five sentences.
Briefly introduce yourself and make a specific connection to the company or its work.
Do enough research to mention a detail that shows genuine interest; Steph gives listening to a prospect's podcast as an example.
Show a relevant portfolio sample and ask to connect.
For UK outreach, check the recipient type and consent rules before sending electronic marketing messages.

quote.text: If you master the art of the cold pitch, right, which really I think comes down to four or five sentences where you are briefly introducing yourself.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

tactics.name: Choose a niche and make an honest personal connection
steps: Review the kinds of writing work available, including books, corporate marketing, blogs, landing pages, ads and scripts.
Choose an area that holds your interest and develop skill in one format so clients can understand what you do.
Use a real connection to the prospect's product or work in the pitch.
Steph gives a beef protein powder brand as an example: she tried the product, sent honest feedback, then asked whether the company needed a writer.

quote.text: I contacted the guy who ran the company. I said, "Hey, I tried this. This flavor is awesome. Like don't stop."
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

tactics.name: Quote projects after gathering scope
steps: Ask how many pages or words the client needs and whether existing copy is available.
Review the current copy to estimate the amount of editing or new writing needed.
If the client agrees, record the discovery call with Granola and use its transcript to check details such as deadlines.
Set a project-based fee after clarifying scope, even if the estimate is informed by an internal hourly calculation.

quote.text: You might even still be calculating it based on like an hourly rate, but there are no surprises. You know that like you know what the scope is.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

tactics.name: Use AI for selected steps in tutorial writing

Use Cursor to route video and audio processing to Gemini and capture the narration and difficult points.

warnings.warning: Steph says trying to automate the whole writing process can consume time configuring and maintaining tools, still produce imperfect work, and leave writers burned out.
She says not to rely on AI for all writing: it can flatten a writer's voice and prevent the writer's thinking and skills from developing.
Steph says not to keyword stuff and advises following SEO best practices.
The host promotes his paid YouTube community during the interview, and an embedded Lease End advertisement appears in the transcript. These are promotional segments, not business ideas.

lessons.lesson: Use AI where it saves meaningful effort, such as processing recordings or producing a first draft, and keep a human responsible for research, judgment and the final edit.

quote.text: You can use it and there's a great way to use it but use it in the place you need it the most.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Direct experience with a product gives an article details that a generic AI draft may miss.

quote.text: I am signing up for the tools that I'm writing about. I'm noodling around in them, just clicking, seeing what my experience is like.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: A portfolio can be built without waiting for a paid client or formal certification; self-directed samples can demonstrate ability.

quote.text: With this you just go write the thing. Who's stopping you? No one is stopping you.

lessons.lesson: A clear niche makes it easier for a client to understand why they should hire a freelancer.

quote.text: I think I started as a generalist and it took me a a bit of time to realize, all right, I need to get good at one form
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Tailored pitches work better when they show genuine familiarity with the prospect rather than generic flattery.

quote.text: You're making some sort of connection to something that person does that you like that you genuinely like
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Use a good first project to build trust and offer related work that can extend the contract.

quote.text: once you have a good working relationship it's really easy to make a contract last even years which which I've done.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Clarify project scope before quoting so the client and freelancer know what is included and avoid surprises.

quote.text: It just feels better for everyone involved. I think that's my preference.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Distinctive human experience and personal voice can make writing more engaging than content that follows an expected formula.

quote.text: because they want a a well-rounded person who's tapped into culture, who's going to pull from these rich experiences and put that into the writing cuz that's our advantage as humans.
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: Learning to write clearly remains useful even when AI tools are available, because people still value original thinking and articulation.

quote.text: staying focused is an art learning how to be articulate is an art but that's exactly why people are paying so much for content right now
quote.speaker: Steph Spectre

lessons.lesson: When using an AI-generated reply for a real person, treat it as additional capacity and keep human responsibility for the relationship.

quote.text: So it's additive. It's not replaceive. Right. Right.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest describes her own freelance work, rates, workload, client acquisition and writing process in detail. Most financial and performance figures are personal claims without contracts or independent verification; the AI model-training rate is second-hand, and the host's trend and platform claims are not substantiated in the transcript.
